newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ended lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ended lower.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended lower across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.

"Treasury bill yields ended mixed but bond prices eased slightly today but it did not have an impact on the market. The interbank rate, on the other hand, rose slightly. Volume was only moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 0.95/0.90 percent compared with Friday's yield of 1.13/1.08 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.83/1.78 percent against 1.70/1.65 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.55/98.60 from Friday's close of S$98.80/98.85, September 2001 at S$97.30/97.35 versus S$97.75/97.80 and June 2003 at S$95.33/95.38 against S$95.70/95.75
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-3/8, 2-1/4 percent from Friday's 1-0/0, 0-7/8 percent.
